boundaries: the key state each member reads

notes: History a group turns on later. One pass, no finding; B3 added the HTTP test the route lacked, and G4 rebuilt one control this change made stale. Two older controls were already stale at the base and are named in G4.

instruments.evidence: History a group turns on later: POST /groups/:id/keys/history and ShareHistory (8a8a2b733), and the send sharing missing versions when the key is current (cbd34c40a). Boundaries: the history request, the group_key_members rows, the key state each member reads.
Read ff5386434 (G4b/G4c/G5; its I1 row named this exact gap as not delivered) and f4de50ef6, whose control g3c2a covers the send path this change edits.

Printed the history request for three states in the send tests: history visible with a held version (shared), hidden (nothing sent), a refused share (logged, message unaffected). Rotation history stays as G5 left it.

Nothing had sent the route real HTTP: added TestGroupKeyHistoryRouteOverHTTP (0e5c55da4). Through the router the server builds, the app's JSON -- version and member ids as object keys, arriving as strings -- binds; hidden history answers 400 group_key_history_not_allowed; shown, 204; the member's GET then returns both versions.
The stored row read back through the member's key state: key_version 1 with the shared copy, beside version 2.
The route and body match on both sides: /groups/{id}/keys/history, {history: {version: {member: copy}}} -- proven by the HTTP test sending the client's shape.
The app reads nothing from the 204; the member reads its copies through the existing key state.
One rule for older copies (checkGroupKeyHistory) and one insert loop (insertGroupKeyHistory), used by the rotation and the share alike.
The contract with the other end was driven over HTTP (B3), not assumed from the service test.
No field added to a struct that crosses a boundary; the request is a new struct with one tagged field.
Integer map keys from JSON strings are decoded by encoding/json; the HTTP test exercises exactly that.
The HTTP test sends the body shape the app builds, not a Go-typed request.
A version held by the sender and lacked by a member is shared.
Refused: hidden history, a non-member, a version the sender does not hold, a member who lacks nothing, a second copy of the same version, an empty body.
Empty history is refused before a transaction starts.
The sibling is the rotation, which already carries history; the share uses its exact checks and lock.
Every refusal branch is reached by the service test.
A refused share is logged and retried on the next send; the message is never affected (tested).
Both paths gate on history_visible, tested both ways.
The insert loop was extracted rather than copied.
Other places older copies could be written: only the rotation and this route.
No goroutine or shared memory; concurrency is settled by the row lock.
One transaction: a failed insert rolls back every copy of the share.
A share leaves only copies that belong to current members; nothing to undo.
No finding, so no new control. g3c2a (f4de50ef6) was made stale by the new branch in groupKeyForSending and is rebuilt; it fails as it did when recorded: expected 1 call, got 2.
The share runs on every group send whose key is current; nothing to invoke.
go build, vet, gofmt clean; golangci-lint 0 issues on services, handlers, integration, cmd/server; tsc -b 0; eslint and prettier clean.

Not run in a browser: it needs a group and a pane with a repaired key pair, neither of which exists. The server half is proven over HTTP against the real database; the device half by tests with real RSA for the rewrap (a5b85e58f).
The share starts beside the send and nothing waits on it.
Known-bad inputs refused, as D2 lists.
Services group key tests 10 passed; integration group key tests 4 passed; handlers group tests ok; frontend 12 files, 149 passed; nothing skipped.
Closes the limit ff5386434 recorded: history turned on later now reaches existing members, at the next send by a member who holds the versions -- not instantly, and not in a group where nobody sends.

Two devices, or two sends, sharing the same copy at once: the second waits for the conversation row lock, then finds nothing missing and is refused (tested: 'a second copy of the same version is refused').

Every test naming the changed modules in src and tests (groupKeyCache, groupKeysService, groupKeys): 12 files, all pass. Go: the group key service tests, the four group key HTTP tests, the handlers' group tests.
The shared test router gained the one route; the whole group key integration set ran on it.

Re-applied every control that patches a changed file: g1d, g2b, groupkeycache-unwrap-never-proven and it-skip-without-variable apply; g3c2a was stale and is rebuilt; g1b-key-state-open-to-non-members and rl-mod-mail-unlimited were already stale at the base 9cc07e6b7, before this change -- left as found and named here.
